answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to costly, time-locked stake instead of free accounts. Require every agent to lock a non-trivial deposit that only unlocks after many epochs, so spawning a thousand clones multiplies the attacker cost linearly while an honest agent pays once. Like filling a canyon one terrace at a time, the defense compounds: the old fable of unlimited free identities collapses when every fake peer demands real capital, making large sybil swarms economically irrational.
